rationale: Extending the measured coverage of the accepted-then-panicking configuration change from one explicit transition value to both. EnterJoint treats JointImplicit as a joint transition just like JointExplicit, so the same empty change set with JointImplicit should be accepted by propose-time validation and then panic on apply; a local run of the extended harness confirms exactly that (leave_joint false, enter_joint_ok true, the proposal step returning no error and leaving an EntryConfChangeV2, and applyConfChange panicking with config is already joint while still joint), while the Auto control in the same invocation leaves the joint configuration with no panic. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation so the controller can produce the receipt; the assertion already recorded is unchanged and this broadens the condition under which the defect is reachable.

scope.description: Cover both non-Auto transition values for the empty-change-set panic: the explicit transition already measured, the implicit transition added here, and the Auto control, all against the same joint configuration in one invocation.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and library defaults; the joint configuration is entered identically in each case with ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]}.
The implicit case submits ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit} with zero changes through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, which is the same input shape as the explicit case.
ApplyConfChange is invoked directly in each case because a quorum-less instance cannot commit; the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data and no production logic is modified.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; only the library's transition values are compared.
Non-joint configurations, which validation already rejects with a log message and an entry rewrite.

experiment.prefix: The harness now runs three cases over the same joint entry. TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint and TestAssuranceEmptyImplicitConfChangeJoint build newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promote it, apply the explicit-transition EnterJoint change, and emit a setup event naming the tested transition together with joint state, voters, voters_outgoing, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint. Each then marshals its empty ConfChangeV2 into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, emits the step error, appended count and last entry type, and finally applies that change inside a recover, emitting whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint. TestAssuranceEmptyAutoConfChangeLeavesJoint is the control and emits the same shape with joint_after and voters_after.

comparisons.description: The implicit-transition empty change is also accepted by validation rather than replaced, so the trigger is not specific to JointExplicit.
The implicit-transition empty change panics on apply exactly like the explicit one, because EnterJoint accepts it as a joint transition while the configuration is already joint.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passed validation and panicked on apply while the Auto form left the joint configuration without panicking
validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition
